step.text: I'll look at how the browser panel renders files today.

The build pipeline uses `--publish never` for the dmg and exe artifacts, then uploads them to GitHub releases via `gh release create`. For electron-updater to work properly, I need the metadata files like `latest-mac.yml` and `latest.yml` published alongside the artifacts—these are generated by electron-builder when the publish config is set up correctly.

On macOS, electron-updater requires the app to be signed and needs a `.zip` target in addition to the dmg (the dmg alone isn't sufficient for auto-updates). On Windows, the nsis target is needed, which should already be the default. The mac target currently only specifies "dmg", so I need to add "zip" to it. The workflow references CSC_LINK secrets, suggesting the app is being signed, but if it's unsigned the updates will fail with a code signature error.

I also need to add a `publish` configuration to package.json that points to the GitHub repository for electron-updater to know where to check for releases. For the UI, I'm thinking about where to surface the "Update available" notification — it should be persistent like a pill or chip in the top bar rather than a toast, since an update is a record that needs to stay visible. I should check the renderer structure to see where this fits best, and verify whether electron-updater is already available in node_modules.

There are no releases yet, so this is the initial OTA setup with version 0.1.0. I'm going to examine the top bar, how the renderer communicates with the main process through the preload API, and the toast system by reading through some files. I'm thinking about splitting the work—I'll handle the main process updater, package.json publish config, workflow adjustments, preload wiring, and renderer UI, while delegating the helper tasks for parts that don't touch my files.

The tricky part is figuring out what's actually separable. Writing integration tests before the module exists is risky, and the workflow changes and package.json config overlap with what I need to do anyway. I could have a helper write the test suite after I define the module shape, but that won't run until the module exists. Instead, I'll do most of this myself and have a helper focus on pure research—figuring out exactly what electron-updater needs for macOS (signed zip, latest-mac.yml) and confirming version and target requirements by reading the docs and node_modules. That's read-only work with no file conflicts.

Actually, a cleaner split: have a helper handle just the CI workflow file in `.github/workflows/build.yml` since I won't touch that file at all. I'll write the package.json publish config and give the helper exact instructions on what to assume. First I need to check the renderer code to understand the UI shape, then I can give helpers clear, complete instructions.
